content.thinking:
Since notice was given on 10 October, the required two months' notice means the earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026, unless the landlord agrees in writing to a shorter period.

My plan is to reply to the tenant confirming the earliest possible end date, notify the landlord to get their decision on whether to approve an earlier end, and hold off on confirming keys drop-off or deposit timing until that end date is settled -- I'll note deposit return typically happens within 10 days of agreement per the scheme, but I won't promise specifics prematurely.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and good luck with the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 a tenant needs to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Your email of 10 October means the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026, and you remain responsible for rent until then.

You can leave sooner only if your landlord agrees in writing. I'm asking him now whether he'd agree to 10 November, or another date. I can't promise he will, and until he does, 10 December stands. Please don't hand back keys or treat 10 November as agreed yet.

Keys: we'll confirm where and when to return them once the end date is settled. Please keep them until then.

Deposit: your £2,019 is held in the mydeposits scheme. It's returned after the tenancy ends and we've done a check-out and agreed any deductions. I can't give a date yet, but we'll explain the steps once your end date is confirmed.

You'll hear from us again by Wednesday 14 October.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

options: Keep to 10 Dec 2026 (no agreement needed; we start marketing and arrange check-out) - recommended default
Agree in writing to end on 10 Nov 2026 (rent due to that date only)
Agree to another date of your choosing, e.g. if a replacement tenant is found sooner

Invalid as short; two months applies (RRA 2025), earliest end 10 Dec 2026 unless landlord agrees earlier in writing. Tenant and landlord informed. content.thinking:
Since notice was given on 10 October, the required two months' notice means the earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026, unless the landlord agrees in writing to a shorter period.

My plan is to reply to the tenant confirming the earliest possible end date, notify the landlord to get their decision on whether to approve an earlier end, and hold off on confirming keys drop-off or deposit timing until that end date is settled -- I'll note deposit return typically happens within 10 days of agreement per the scheme, but I won't promise specifics prematurely.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and good luck with the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 a tenant needs to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Your email of 10 October means the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026, and you remain responsible for rent until then.

You can leave sooner only if your landlord agrees in writing. I'm asking him now whether he'd agree to 10 November, or another date. I can't promise he will, and until he does, 10 December stands. Please don't hand back keys or treat 10 November as agreed yet.

Keys: we'll confirm where and when to return them once the end date is settled. Please keep them until then.

Deposit: your £2,019 is held in the mydeposits scheme. It's returned after the tenancy ends and we've done a check-out and agreed any deductions. I can't give a date yet, but we'll explain the steps once your end date is confirmed.

You'll hear from us again by Wednesday 14 October.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

options: Keep to 10 Dec 2026 (no agreement needed; we start marketing and arrange check-out) - recommended default
Agree in writing to end on 10 Nov 2026 (rent due to that date only)
Agree to another date of your choosing, e.g. if a replacement tenant is found sooner
